metadata.title: DWP cuts warning as major benefits shake-up could leave claimants with less cash
metadata.contentSnippet: Alan Milburn's welfare review could mean some under-25s receive less in DWP benefits, with stricter new rules for those refusing work or training.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: DWP cuts warning as major benefits shake-up could leave claimants with less cash
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Some young people could see their benefits cut under a major DWP shake-up, with those who refuse offers of work, training or employment support potentially losing financial help. Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden has confirmed that some young people will receive less financial support in future under recommendations expected in a major review of youth unemployment. Former Labour health secretary Alan Milburn is due to publish his independent report on Tuesday, November 17, setting out proposals to tackle the growing number of 16 to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training (Neets), which topped one million this year. One of the biggest proposals is reported to be to move some young people currently receiving health-related benefits onto a new 'youth allowance', paid at the standard rate of Universal Credit. Mr Milburn has acknowledged that some young people would receive less financial support under his plans. Those who refuse a proposed legal guarantee of work, training or employment support could also risk losing their benefits. Mr Milburn is also expected to recommend gradually cutting the employer National Insurance contributions paid on workers aged 21 to 24 over five years, initially focusing on retail and hospitality. According to the BBC, the plans would double the threshold at which businesses start paying employer National Insurance on earnings from this age group, from £5,000 to £10,000. However, the changes would only be introduced "when economic conditions allow". Mr Milburn is expected to argue that a blanket cut would not be the best use of the several billion pounds of public money it could cost, particularly if young people cannot find jobs after gaining new skills. Mr McFadden has backed the proposed legal guarantee, arguing that employment support needs a stronger legal foundation and would give young people "more certainty about what they're entitled to". Speaking to Sky News' Sunday Morning programme, he said the Government needed to make changes not "in spite of being Labour people", but "because we're Labour people". "It's a different proposition from last year, and I hope that Parliament views it in that light," he said. The Government will be hoping to avoid another Labour rebellion after ministers were forced to water down proposed welfare cuts last year. Shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said the legal entitlement "might sound a nice thing to do" but "doesn't make sense". However, she described the move away from "handing out cash for relatively mild conditions" and towards employment support as "the right direction of travel". Reform UK's Danny Kruger said he was "encouraged" by "the suggestion that we need to be much stricter about benefits for young people who should be supported into work or should be working". Recommended reading: The review is also expected to call for the proportion of children considered school-ready at the start of reception to rise from 75% to 90%. Mr Milburn is expected to warn that too many five-year-olds struggle with everyday tasks such as using cutlery or going to the toilet. He has previously warned that tackling youth unemployment could take a decade and billions of pounds, arguing that "crude cuts" would simply result in young people appearing elsewhere in Government spending figures.

metadata.title: Great British Bake Off star set to return to TV with special Christmas show
metadata.contentSnippet: Dame Mary Berry is returning to TV with a festive BBC special featuring a star-studded line-up of guests.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Great British Bake Off star set to return to TV with special Christmas show
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Great British Bake Off Star is set to return to screens with a new festive cooking special. Mary Berry’s Christmas Countdown will air on BBC One and iPlayer, featuring a star-studded line=u of Miranda Hart, Alexandra Burke and Greg James. The one-hour programme will count down the top 15 most searched-for festive recipes on BBC Food. Dame Mary said: "Christmas is such a special time of year, and food has always been at the heart of how we celebrate. "I’ve loved looking back at my recipes that have become festive favourites over the years. "From traditional classics to delicious treats, there’s something for everyone to enjoy. "I hope this programme inspires viewers to get into the Christmas spirit and perhaps discover a new family favourite along the way." The BBC said the show will feature "timeless Christmas classics" alongside "unexpected festive gems," with recipes that viewers return to "year after year." Ms Hart, who competed on Celebrity Traitors earlier this year, said: "Dame Mary is gentle, kind, fun, light-hearted and sparkling which is exactly what Christmas is all about. "Mary Berry IS Christmas! "To chat and giggle with her was such a treat, plus she pulled off a miracle – she got me looking forward to doing some cooking this Christmas!" The show will celebrate more than just food, highlighting the broader joys of the season—from school plays and outings to stocking fillers and family traditions. Among the recipes featured will be Christmas pudding, chocolate roulade and gingerbread. Ms Burke described the experience as "a joy and dream come true to spend time with Mary," while Mr James said "baking next to the woman that basically invented cakes was such a treat." Ricky Cooper, BBC commissioning editor of factual entertainment and events, said Dame Mary has spent more than 60 years "teaching the nation how to cook mouthwatering recipes that have become beloved staples of family Christmases everywhere." Dame Mary has published more than 75 cookery books and hosted numerous BBC series. Recommended reading She served as a judge on The Great British Bake Off from 2010 until 2016. Mary Berry’s Christmas Countdown will air soon on BBC One and iPlayer. Will you be watching Mary Berry's Christmas Countdown this year? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: I’m A Celebrity stars face gruelling trials in first look at brand new 2026 series
metadata.contentSnippet: I’m A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here! returns to ITV1, STV and ITVX, as Wayne Rooney, Joanna Page and Ricky Wilson face gruelling jungle trials in Australia.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: I’m A Celebrity stars face gruelling trials in first look at brand new 2026 series
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: I’m A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here! returns to ITV1 on Monday with a new lineup of stars. The ITV reality series, hosted by Ant McPartlin and Dec Donnelly, sees celebrities take on gruelling trials and jungle life in Australia as they compete for meals. This year’s cast includes former footballer Wayne Rooney, actress Joanna Page, model Leomie Anderson, Kaiser Chiefs frontman Ricky Wilson, Paralympian and TV presenter Ade Adepitan, content creator Sharky, TV presenter AJ Odudu, and comedian Jack Skipper. They are joined by TV personality and radio DJ Chloe Burrows, soap star Claire Sweeney, and broadcaster Mariella Frostrup. Gavin and Stacey star Joanna Page is seen in the first episode speeding through the Australian wilderness in a buggy before meeting Wilson and Sharky, who describes it as "the car from hell." Sweeney and Anderson soon join them before Ant and Dec arrive. Dec said: "The niceties end here, because from this moment on you’re all in direct competition with one another. "You’re about to face a challenge where there will be serious consequences for the loser." Ant then reveals the first trial. He said: "This truck is about to become your worst nightmare, because one at a time, you each have to scale it, scramble around the outside of it, whilst locating and igniting three flares, all whilst going around these tracks at speed. "If you complete it you’ll win a meal for camp tonight." Meanwhile, on the Gold Coast, the remaining six celebrities begin their jungle journey with buggy rides down the beach. Wayne Rooney, however, starts the adventure from above, taking part in a skydive. He said: "Of my whole career, this is probably my most vulnerable… out of the whole show this is my biggest fear." Ade Adepitan, who is a wheelchair user, shares his mindset ahead of the challenge. He said: "My everyday life I live out of my comfort zone, why is the jungle going to be any harder? "I’ll give it everything I’ve got." After completing his skydive, Adepitan kisses the ground and dedicates the moment to his son. The group later reunites at a rooftop bar in a luxury hotel, where they are presented with their first jungle challenge. Waiters serve them "prawn-star martinis"—giant cocktails made of fermented prawns and blended fish eyes. Ant explains that at the bottom of each glass is a different safe word, and that they must drain the glass using a straw to suck out the fluid and spit it into the bucket next to the glass. Last year’s series was won by social media star AngryGinge, whose real name is Morgan Burtwistle. I’m A Celebrity... Get Me Out Of Here! starts on Monday at 9pm on ITV1, STV, and ITVX.

metadata.title: Environmental disaster fears after 14,000 litres of oil dumped in ditch off A14
metadata.contentSnippet: Calls for urgent action to avert an environmental disaster have been made after an estimated 14,000 litres of waste engine oil was dumped into a Huntingdonshire ditch.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Environmental disaster fears after 14,000 litres of oil dumped in ditch off A14
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Calls for urgent action to avert an environmental disaster have been made after an estimated 14,000 litres of waste engine oil was dumped into a Huntingdonshire ditch. Robert Neilson has raised concerns after being alerted to the illegal 'fly-tipping' by a family member who farms the area off the A14 between the Leighton Bromswold and Catworth junctions. Mr Neilson, who lives in Ramsey, said his relative found the oil while working on the farm earlier this week. “He told me he contacted the Environment Agency straight away because he was so concerned about the amount of oil and the environmental disaster it could cause,” said Mr Neilson. He said Environment Agency officers had visited the site, but no action had yet been taken to clear the mess. “I have been told the Environment Agency estimates that it's between six or seven tanker loads of the used engine oil that's been dumped – around 14,000 litres. This is not an accident. You don't accidentally dump that much oil into a ditch,” said Mr Neilson. He is worried that without action, the oil will make its way into the River Ouse at Huntingdon. Mr Neilson said the ditch currently contains little water, so the oil is not moving much, although some has reached a nearby brook. But heavy rain could send water from the A14 into the ditch, giving the oil enough water to reach the River Ouse. “This is an environmental disaster waiting to happen. That amount of oil is going to have a massive impact on the wildlife; it will kill fish and affect birds and other animals,” said Mr Neilson. He said the Environment Agency needed to act quickly before rain, adding that a digger could scoop most of the oil from the ditch. "Obviously someone has come along into the layby with their tanker full of oil and simply opened the tap. It was probably done after dark so no one would probably take much notice, and think it was someone parked up for a nap," said Mr Neilson, who added: "This is absolutely disgusting. It is vandalism, and the worst kind of fly-tipping and action is needed pronto." An Environment Agency spokesperson said: "We've installed barriers to help protect Ellington Brook from the appalling dumping of oil on the A14 and are advising National Highways on clean-up measures to limit the environmental impacts." The spokesperson added that National Highways is leading the clean-up and, where appropriate, can take enforcement action where its drainage network has been misused. The police are responsible for investigating any suspected criminal activity and can support Environment Agency investigations through measures such as CCTV and ANPR enquiries.

metadata.title: Russell Brand shares message after he was reportedly moved to Cambridgeshire prison
metadata.contentSnippet: Laura Gallacher has shared a message from her husband Russell Brand, who was reportedly moved to HMP Littlehey in Huntingdon last week.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Russell Brand shares message after he was reportedly moved to Cambridgeshire prison
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Laura Gallacher has shared a message from her husband Russell Brand, who has served the first week of his 10-and-a-half-year prison sentence for rape and sexual assault. The disgraced comedian was jailed this week after being found guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others during his career. He was reportedly moved from HMP Wandsworth in London to HMP Littlehey, near Huntingdon, last week, according to The Sun on Sunday. The prison offers a large variety of extra-curricular activities for its inmates, including yoga, choir and indoor bowls. Earlier this year Brand and Gallacher began releasing a weekly YouTube podcast called Sunday Service, which they carried on recording throughout his trial. On Sunday, Gallacher released another episode which began with her reading a passage from Brand’s bible. The 39-year-old, who is the daughter of Ryder Cup-winning golfer Bernard Gallacher, said during the episode: “Russell has asked me to read something to you.” Reading the message from a notebook, she went on: “Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. “As you know, I am not guilty for the offences I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening. “The good news is that Christ is with us when we choose him, and I do. “I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey, little as in small, and hey as in hey, I’m in the biggest sex offenders’ prison in Europe. “The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated. “And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone. “I don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that Christ died to save, like you and me, let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as God forgave us.” Gallacher choked up as she said: “Please support my treasured wife and family. I feel your prayers, your brother in Christ. Russell.” She began the episode by saying she is here to “continue the good work that was being established here in this Sunday service community, something very, very close to mine and Russell’s heart”. “It may look different, but the ambitions are very much the same, and we trust God, and we trust his plan, and we trust everything he’s doing right now,” she added. “Even though it’s painful, and obviously, will take some getting used to for me to even sit here and not have my companion and my person with me, but I want to continue, and I’m grateful for the support.” Gallacher said she is speaking to her husband, adding: “He’s okay, and he’s praying.” Brand was sentenced to a 10-and-a-half-year prison term on Monday afternoon. He is expected to serve two-thirds of his prison sentence before being released on licence. He will be on the sex offenders’ register for life.

news.title: Motorcyclist seriously injured after crash involving Audi in Hunts town
news.content: A motorcyclist has been seriously injured in a crash involving a car in a Huntingdonshire town. Police were called at 4.47pm on Saturday (November 14) to reports of a collision between an Audi Q3 and a motorbike in Great Whyte, Ramsey. Officers and paramedics attended and the motorcyclist was rushed to hospital with serious injuries, Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed. A spokesperson for the force said: "The Audi driver was unhurt and remained at the scene. "An investigation is ongoing, and anyone with information should contact us via the website or 101 quoting incident 360 of November 14." Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: Strictly Come Dancing lift rules explained - when are they illegal and the penalties?
metadata.contentSnippet: Strictly Come Dancing lift rules explained, including banned dances, permitted routines, and how judges penalise illegal moves.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Strictly Come Dancing lift rules explained - when are they illegal and the penalties?
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Lifts can create some of the most memorable moments on Strictly Come Dancing, however, they are not allowed in every routine. The rules around lifts are often a source of confusion for viewers, contestants, and even the judges themselves. Here is a guide to what makes a lift illegal on Strictly, which dances allow them, and how the judges handle rule-breakers. A lift is defined as any movement where a dancer has both feet off the floor with assistance or support from their partner. Strictly judge Craig Revel Horwood highlighted the rule in 2024 after Pete Wicks and professional partner Jowita Przystał included two lifts in their Rumba. He said one foot should have remained on the floor and described both moves as "totally illegal", adding that couples could lose marks for doing so. However, the definition relies on whether the airborne movement was supported by the partner, not simply if both feet left the floor. There is some room for interpretation. In 2022, Ellie Simmonds was helped down from a table by Nikita Kuzmin during their Paso Doble. Head judge Shirley Ballas deducted a point for the 'assisted lift', while Revel Horwood said the issue was that it lasted too long. He suggested that a brief, supported descent would have been acceptable. Lifts are banned in the 10 core ballroom and Latin dances featured on Strictly Come Dancing: In these routines, a lift is considered an illegal move. Lifts are permitted in some of the show’s other styles, including: Lifts are banned in the 10 core ballroom and Latin dances on Strictly Come Dancing. (Image: BBC/Guy Levy) They are also allowed in contemporary and jazz routines. American Smooth routines can include lifts, although the exact number permitted may vary based on the show’s current rules. Performing an illegal lift does not result in automatic disqualification. Instead, judges have the option to deduct points. In 2022, Ballas clearly stated she was deducting one point from Ellie Simmonds for an assisted lift. Revel Horwood also mentioned marking Dani Dyer and Nikita Kuzmin down during their week 8 routine (Paso Doble) on Strictly 2026 due to the use of illegal lifts. However, enforcement is not always consistent. During Wicks’ 2024 Rumba, Ballas said she would "let them slide", while Revel Horwood insisted they should be marked down and even suggested disqualification. He later admitted this was unlikely, saying the show had "never really disqualified anyone," but stood by the idea that illegal lifts should affect the score. How well do you know the lift rules on Strictly Come Dancing? Let us know in the comments below.

metadata.title: UK health drink company sold at Holland & Barrett saved after entering administration
metadata.contentSnippet: Deeply Foods, a gut-health drink brand stocked by Holland & Barrett, has been saved after falling into administration earlier this month.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK health drink company sold at Holland & Barrett saved after entering administration
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A UK health drink company stocked at Holland & Barrett has been rescued after collapsing into administration. Deeply Foods, established in 2021, is a UK gut-health brand specialising in prebiotic fibre drinks. Created by nutritionists, Deeply drinks are designed to boost fibre intake and support gut health. Deeply Foods products are available on the company's website and from retailers across the UK, including Holland & Barrett and Whole Foods Market. The prebiotic fibre drinks come in two flavours: Deeply Foods, on its website, said: "90% of us aren't getting enough fibre in our diet. "Most of us struggle to get anywhere near, with the average person in the UK consuming less than 20g. "That's why we created Deeply." After five years in business, Deeply Foods entered administration earlier this month. Paul Ellison and Christopher Errington of KRE Corporate Recovery Limited were appointed joint administrators on November 5, according to The Gazette. But Deeply has now been rescued in a pre-pack sale, securing the brand's future. The company will continue under new ownership after being acquired by a family office investor through a deal with administrators. Majority shareholder, Jonty Shepard, said: "We see enormous potential in the Deeply brand. "Our priority is to build on the foundations already established, focus on what makes the brand unique and develop the business sustainably for the long term." The new owners plan to focus on the brand’s core strengths and long-term growth. Co-founder Mark Tanous will return to an operational role to help guide the brand’s next steps. He will work closely with the new owners to strengthen Deeply’s market position and support a focused and sustainable growth strategy. It has been a tough year for the UK high street, with several retailers entering administration or liquidation and others announcing widespread store closures. Major high street brands Claire's and Quiz have been forced to close all their remaining stores after falling into administration. UK fashion retailer Leading Labels is also set to close its remaining 15 stores after falling into liquidation in May. Whitbread closed all its standalone branded restaurants across the UK last month, affecting five brands: However, Queensway Inns and Common Table Group have now taken over 110 of these former Whitbread sites, saving them from closure. Poundland has filed a notice to appoint administrators, putting the future of its 150 stores and 11,000 employees at risk. TG Jones and the British Heart Foundation will also be closing around 150 stores each across the UK. Wynsors World of Shoes is shutting 17 stores across the UK, with closing down sales already underway at several affected branches. UK entertainment retailer Zavvi has ceased trading after nearly 20 years, having collapsed into administration for a second time. Australian stationery retailer Typo is also set to pull out of the UK in 2027, closing all its stores and ending online trading. Other retailers have been forced to close stores this year, including: Several UK travel companies have ceased trading or entered administration in 2026, including: Wayfairer Travel Limited has also suspended all services "until further notice" as it looks to appoint an administrator. Meanwhile, four UK airlines have fallen into administration or liquidation: Meanwhile, UK delivery company Yodel was phased out completely in July after being acquired by InPost. Iconic fashion brand Nasty Gal has also shut down its website after being sold by Debenhams in a deal worth around £12 million (US$16 million). It hasn't all been bad news for the UK high street, with several major brands announcing new store openings for 2026, including Joules, B&M, Aldi, M&S, and Superdrug. Meanwhile, brands including Evans and Bodycare have returned to the UK high street this year after previously closing all their stores. Have you tried Deeply Foods drinks before? metadata.title: UK motorists urged not to ignore this common night-time driving problem
metadata.contentSnippet: An optician explains why drivers should get glare or blurred lights checked and shares five tips for driving after dark.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK motorists urged not to ignore this common night-time driving problem
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Drivers who see blurred headlights or halos around lights are being urged to get their eyesight checked. Adam Aslam, director at Nevies Opticians, said changes in vision can be particularly noticeable when motorists are driving after dark. He said streaks, glare and blurred lights can have different causes and advised people whose sight is affected to ask an optometrist for advice. One possible cause is astigmatism, a common condition that can make headlights, streetlights and road signs appear blurred or distorted, particularly at night. The NHS says astigmatism can cause blurred vision, headaches and eye strain, and recommends visiting an optician if someone has symptoms. It explains that astigmatism means the eye is shaped more like a rugby ball than a football, causing light to focus in more than one place in the eye. It says the condition does not always need treatment, but glasses or contact lenses are among the options. The NHS also advises going to an optician if you have not had an eye test for two years, and says regular tests are important. Mr Aslam said: “Many people assume everyone sees headlights the same way they do, so they may not realise there could be an issue with their vision. “If lights appear unusually bright, blurry or surrounded by halos, it’s worth booking an eye examination to have your vision checked.” Even motorists with healthy vision can find driving after dark more challenging during the winter months, according to the optician. He also shared five ways motorists can prepare for journeys in low light, including cleaning the inside as well as the outside of their windscreen. Dust, residue and condensation on the glass can scatter light and make glare from oncoming headlights worse, he said. His advice is to clean both sides regularly and clear condensation before setting off. Mr Aslam also recommends avoiding a bright phone screen just before a journey and giving your eyes a moment to adjust to the dark. He advises drivers not to use their phones while driving. Changes in driving habits can be worth noticing, too. According to Mr Aslam, of Nevies Opticians, avoiding unfamiliar routes or driving after dark, slowing down more than usual and relying heavily on road markings can be signs that vision has changed. Anyone who has adapted their behaviour in these ways should consider an eye test, he said. Repeated star-shaped lights, streaks or halos should not simply be assumed to be normal, particularly if they affect how clearly someone can see. Motorists should also check that they have the right lights on, as daytime running lights often do not illuminate the rear of a car, according to Mr Aslam. He recommends switching headlights on in poor visibility and using dipped beam when other road users are nearby. The Highway Code advises drivers dazzled by oncoming headlights to slow down and, if necessary, stop. Mr Aslam added: “People routinely service their cars, check their tyres and replace worn wipers, yet many overlook their eyesight. “Your vision plays a huge role in how safely you drive, particularly during the darker months. “If you’ve noticed changes in your sight, booking an eye test is a sensible step.”

metadata.title: Popular Greek island airport closes for 4 months with all flights cancelled
metadata.contentSnippet: Chios Airport has been closed today (Sunday, November 15, 2026) until March 15, 2027, due to a runway upgrade, with all flights cancelled.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Popular Greek island airport closes for 4 months with all flights cancelled
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Greek airport has been closed for four months, with all flights to and from the popular island cancelled. Chios is Greece's fifth-biggest island with a population of around 50,300 residents, while the local airport welcomes more than 300,000 passengers each year. However, Chios National Airport Omiros has now been closed until March so work can be carried out on the runway. Chios Airport closed on Sunday (November 15) and won't reopen again until March 15, 2027. The closure is due to work that will extend and upgrade the runway ahead of next summer’s tourist season, according to the Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority. All flights to and from Chios have been cancelled until March 15. Only emergency flights, including medical evacuations and search and rescue, can land during the work. The runway is currently 1,511 metres long, so wide-bodied aircraft cannot land. It handles smaller propeller planes and narrow-body aircraft, meaning visitors must fly to Athens or Thessaloniki before taking a smaller connection to Chios. After the project, it will measure 1,799 metres and accept much larger aircraft. Airlines including SKY Express and Aegean offer connecting flights to Chios Airport from several major UK airports, including: British travellers heading to Chios during the closure can fly to Athens, before travelling to the island by ferry from Piraeus. Ferries are also available from destinations including Lesvos and Çeşme in Turkey. Not everyone is happy about the runway upgrade, with the work at Chios Airport facing opposition. President of the Chios chamber of commerce, Pantelis Legatos, said: "The early closure will seriously affect the economy and society of the island, especially during the holiday season (Christmas, New Year), when people have planned trips, family visits and medical appointments. "Chios, as a border island 5 miles from Turkey, depends on the air connection with the capital for health, entertainment and freedom reasons." Does the Chios Airport closure impact your travel plans? metadata.title: WhatsApp users warned this group chat mistake could lead to criminal charges
metadata.contentSnippet: WhatsApp users across the UK face new pornographic image laws (introduced on November 6) - see how they could land users with criminal charges.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: WhatsApp users warned this group chat mistake could lead to criminal charges
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A simple mistake in a WhatsApp group chat could leave people facing criminal charges under new laws, a legal expert has warned. Ruth Peters from Olliers Solicitors said an image automatically saved from a group chat can lead to serious charges, even if the recipient did not ask for it. New offences covering possession and publication of specified pornographic images came into force in England and Wales on November 6 under the Crime and Policing Act 2026. They do not apply to every explicit image, and receiving an unsolicited image does not automatically mean someone has committed an offence. But those found in breach of the new laws could find themselves facing criminal charges and time in jail. The new rules cover pornography that explicitly and realistically depicts strangulation or suffocation, certain incest-themed penetrative sexual activity, or sexual activity involving someone who is, or is pretending to be, under 16. The people depicted must appear to a reasonable person to be real, according to government guidance. Whether someone possesses an image is a question of fact for a court, but the guidance says it could include material stored on a device, in a personal account or in cloud storage. The maximum sentence for possession is two years for material depicting strangulation or suffocation or certain relatives, and three years for material depicting someone who is, or is pretending to be, under 16. Publication carries a maximum sentence of five years for all three offences. Ms Peters said Olliers Solicitors had encountered around 10 current or ongoing cases in which people faced serious consequences after images from group chats were found on their phones. She recalled a case involving an image of bestiality found during a phone examination in an unrelated investigation that resulted in no further action. The Disclosure and Barring Service dealt with the image offence with a caution, but was subsequently considering whether to place the person on a barred list, potentially affecting their employment, she said. Ms Peters said: “The important thing is to understand that possession can be a continuing act. “It is not necessarily about whether you actively went looking for something or whether you downloaded it yourself. “People need to be aware of what is on their devices and understand that images shared in group chats can have serious consequences.” WhatsApp users found breaking the new laws could find themselves facing criminal charges and time in jail. (Image: Yui Mok/PA Wire) The Ministry of Justice says possession can be a continuing act and advises people to permanently delete or otherwise get rid of images covered by the offences. WhatsApp users may have a defence if they were sent an image without asking for it and did not keep it for an unreasonable length of time. There may also be a defence if they had not seen the image before and did not know or have cause to suspect that it was covered by the offences. Ms Peters said: “People arrested for offences where the police need to examine their phones will often have their devices checked by officers. “An image automatically saved from a group chat can lead to very serious charges. “While receiving an image you have not asked for is not necessarily an offence, if that image stays on your device for a period of time, you could potentially face prosecution. “Even if you didn't specifically opt to save that image, it may still remain on your device.” Were you aware of the new pornographic image laws introduced earlier this month? Let us know in the poll above or in the comments below.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Who left Strictly Come Dancing this week? Seventh celebrity out of BBC show
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Another week of the Strictly Come Dancing competition means another celebrity has been eliminated. Will Best and Dianne Buswell narrowly missed out on the Blackpool special after being eliminated in tonight’s (November 15) results show. The Big Brother presenter, 41, and his professional dance partner, 37, scored 27 for their paso doble to Smalltown Boy by Bronski Beat on Saturday’s live show. They found themselves at the bottom of the judges’ leaderboard alongside Graeme Hall and Lauren Oakley, as well as Lacey Turner and Vito Coppola, before public votes were counted. In the week eight dance-off, Best and Buswell faced actress Jaime Winstone and Carlos Gu, who had been third on the leaderboard after the judges gave their Charleston to I Can’t Do It Alone by Catherine Zeta-Jones a score of 33. After the dance-off, Winstone and Gu were saved by judges Motsi Mabuse, Shirley Ballas and Craig Revel Horwood while Anton Du Beke chose to save Best and Buswell. Best was told by Ballas on Saturday’s live show that he was one of the programme’s “most consistent” dancers. However, Revel Horwood called the routine “plonky”. Best has presented shows for Channel 4, ITV and the BBC and in 2023 began co-hosting the ITV revival of Big Brother alongside AJ Odudu, who was a Strictly contestant in 2021. They hosted a Celebrity Big Brother spin-off in 2024. He is also a Hits Radio presenter and last month became a father to Sonny with his partner Tobi Rose. Best previously joked he would wear a mankini on the dancefloor if he made it to Blackpool Week. He made the cheeky promise after already dancing shirtless and in his pants during Movie Week. Mr Best said: "Mankini? Has anyone done a mankini before? "I have no idea what people are thinking I might wear, but I've been feeling pretty overdressed for the last few weeks. "Let's release more buttons." Strictly fans will see Best and Buswell join Ellie Taylor on Strictly – It Takes Two on Monday, November 16 at 6.30pm on BBC Two and iPlayer. On Sunday’s results show, the professional dancers performed a romantasy-inspired group number, which featured the voice of The Traitors US host Alan Cumming. Celebrity Traitors winner Sebastian “Bash” Croft performed his new single, Everything Always Now, accompanied by a routine from dancers Julian Caillon and Jowita Przystal. Strictly Come Dancing continues with its Blackpool Tower Ballroom special on Saturday, November 21. Fans can watch all the dances from 6.35pm on BBC One or iPlayer. The next themed week after Blackpool will be Musicals Week, which is scheduled for the week before the semi-final. Who do you think will make it to the Strictly final this year? metadata.title: Residents fear town ‘losing its heart’ as ideas being discussed to boost businesses
metadata.contentSnippet: Residents fear that St Ives in Huntingdonshire is “losing its heart” as updated plans to revitalise the area are being discussed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Residents fear town ‘losing its heart’ as ideas being discussed to boost businesses
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Residents fear an historic market town is “losing its heart” as updated plans to revitalise the area are being discussed. The St Ives Town Team published an updated document suggesting new riverside moorings, pedestrianised streets and an enhanced market area to boost business in the town. A meeting will be held with businesses, organisations and other interested parties next month to share their views. Ben Obese-Jecty, MP for Huntingdon, posted to Facebook that he had met with the St Ives Town Team to discuss how best to “regenerate the heart” of the town. The Conservative MP said pedestrianising Market Hill and Bridge Street could give an “opportunity for businesses to thrive in St Ives”. He said this could create a “community space that would encourage more cafes and restaurants, a bigger market, the filling of empty shop units and making the town centre a destination”. Mr Obese-Jecty said: “Speaking with the Town Team this matches their vision for the town and they were even able to show me existing plans for pedestrianising the centre from some 25 years ago. “The plans look contemporary enough to still work today without really being changed. “I think St Ives has a huge amount of potential, as demonstrated by the recent additions of businesses from Cambridge.” Robert Stevens, who has lived in St Ives for nearly 30 years, said he feels the town needs “more businesses” as he spoke in front of the Townrow department store, advertising a closing down sale. The 70-year-old said: “It’s a shame – I remember 20 years ago when it was still Eaden Lilley. Apart from the loss of shops, it was starting to look a lot better with a lot more eateries and restaurants around. Making it a bit of a foodie place would be a good idea.” Richard Ibbott, area manager for West End DIY, said he had written to Mr Obese-Jecty to object to the pedestrianisation of Bridge Street. The 59-year-old said: “How am I supposed to get deliveries in? They said use your back door – but I don’t have a back door. “They need to improve the town centre, but not by stopping people from getting into the town. Townrow is gone – Poundland is up the creek – even the hairdressers are going.” A 67-year-old man, who did not want to be named, said reading about the controversial plans proposed by Capital and Centric to build homes on car parks, while free car parking was promoted by the combined authority makes you think “you were in an asylum”. He said: “It’s completely bonkers, you’re going to build on car parks while there’s restricted parking in the town centre. We’re going to lose this as a department store – we don’t need any more takeaways, hairdressers or nail salons. “You’re losing the heart of why people come into St Ives – they say they want to make it a destination venue, but what are they going to come in for? “If you come on a Monday the market is almost dead, back in the day the market used to fill the whole town – it was an event, a community event. “It feels like the heart of the town is really struggling and I think it’s a shame when we have such a good resource for bringing people in like the river.”

metadata.title: Hunts shoppers flock to closing down sale for beloved department store
metadata.contentSnippet: Huntingdonshire shoppers flocked to the Townrow St Ives closing down sale this week after it was revealed the department store would be shutting.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hunts shoppers flock to closing down sale for beloved department store
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Huntingdonshire shoppers flocked to a closing down sale this week after it was revealed a beloved department store would be shutting for good. Townrow will be closing its St Ives store after more than a decade in the town. The store, located on Bridge Street, was previously an Eaden Lilley branch before being taken over by Townrow in 2009. The department store chain, which launched in Essex in 1871, sells clothing, shoes, and kitchenware. A photo from Thursday, November 11, shows St Ives shoppers queueing down the street in their masses for the closing down sale. The closing down sale at Townrow attracted masses of shoppers (Image: Lesley Collier) Edward Townrow, managing director, said: "Like many independent retailers, we have faced increasingly challenging trading conditions, rising operating costs and changes in shopping habits. "Despite exploring a number of alternatives, we have regrettably been unable to establish a financially sustainable future for the store in its current form. "What makes this decision particularly difficult is the extraordinary relationship we have with the people of St Ives. "Our customers have been nothing short of wonderful." He also thanked the team behind the store’s success. He said: "They are the heart and soul of the store, and I could not be prouder of them. "Their dedication, professionalism and genuine care for our customers have made Townrow a very special place." Townrow is set to close its St Ives store (Image: Townrow) Residents were asked to share their thoughts on the closure. Judith Brass said: "It's a sad loss for the town. "It's pretty much the only place worth shopping at for ladies. "We have such great eating places in St Ives nowadays, I was hoping the town was on the up so this is a blow." Ms Natalie Flack praised Townrow for stocking “concession brands like Vera Moda, Mango, Radley, Barbour” and said the staff are wonderful. She added: "I hope they get given another chance." However, other residents said they hoped popular chains such as M&S Food took over the premises. Do you have a story you want to share? Contact emily.stevens@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Boys, 13, banned from Cambs city centre after robberies, thefts and assaults
metadata.contentSnippet: Two 13-year-old boys have been handed anti-social behaviour injunctions and banned from Cambridge city centre after months of criminal activity.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Boys, 13, banned from Cambs city centre after robberies, thefts and assaults
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two 13-year-old boys have been handed anti-social behaviour injunctions and banned from a Cambridgeshire city centre after months of criminal activity. The injunctions, issued at Huntingdon Law Courts on Monday, November 11, follow robberies, thefts, and assaults in Cambridge. The orders will remain in place for one year. PC Jake Weldon from the Cambridge Neighbourhood Team said: "We hope these injunctions send a strong message that anti-social behaviour and crime will not be tolerated in Cambridge. "The behaviour of these individuals has had a significant impact on the city and the people who live, work and visit here. "Throughout this process, we have worked closely with our partners to address their behaviour and prevent further offending. "Following several arrests and extensive partnership work, these injunctions put clear boundaries in place to prevent further offending, encourage the boys to make better choices and provide some respite for the community." The boys must not enter Cambridge city centre unless accompanied by an agreed appropriate adult or attending a pre-arranged appointment. They are also banned from mixing with named teenagers unless an appropriate adult supervises them. They must not act in an anti-social manner that causes or is likely to cause harassment, alarm or distress to one or more people. If they breach the terms, they could be arrested.

metadata.title: Bake Off host Noel Fielding 'deeply disturbed' by Russell Brand's crimes
metadata.contentSnippet: The Great British Bake Off host Noel Fielding said he was "horrified" to hear of Russell Brand's crimes and didn't know about them until the public did.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Bake Off host Noel Fielding 'deeply disturbed' by Russell Brand's crimes
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The Great British Bake Off host Noel Fielding said he has had "no contact" with Russell Brand "for many years". Fielding said he "was completely unaware" of Brand's crimes until they were made public. His statement comes after Brand was jailed for 10 and a half years for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. In a statement issued to The Sun, Fielding said: "I was horrified and deeply disturbed to learn of Russell Brand's crimes, which I was completely unaware of until they became public knowledge. "My thoughts are with the women whose courage brought him to justice. "I appeared on TV, radio and live charity shows with him, and whilst we played it up for the cameras and in the media, I considered it a professional relationship, rather than a personal one. "I have had no contact with him for many years. "Looking back at some of the jokes I made alongside him I was appalled. "They were horrible and inappropriate, and I very much regret them." Brand and Fielding appeared together on Channel 4's Big Fat Quiz Of The Year and performed charity gigs together as The Goth Detectives. A new Netflix documentary will tell Brand's story from his rise to international fame to his dramatic fall from grace. Russell Brand: Open Secret uses insiders' voices and delves into archive footage to offer an insight into the downfall of the 51-year-old. It will also explore the Dispatches investigation for Channel 4 in September 2023, alongside The Times and Sunday Times, which led to the women coming forward to complain and ultimately the four convictions against Brand. It will include his criminal trial at Southwark Crown Court. Brand began his career as a TV presenter and comedian and became a Hollywood star, appearing in films such as Forgetting Sarah Marshall, Hop and the Despicable Me franchise. During a two-decade career, he cemented his status in the spotlight through his marriage to singer Katy Perry, and subsequent appearances on TV, radio, stage and podcasts. He is expected to serve two-thirds of his sentence before being released on licence, and will be on the sex offenders' register for life.

metadata.title: Newsquest and Centrepoint launch Christmas campaign to support homeless young people
metadata.contentSnippet: Newsquest and Centrepoint have launched a Christmas campaign to support young people facing homelessness.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Newsquest and Centrepoint launch Christmas campaign to support homeless young people
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Newsquest, the UK's largest local media group, and Centrepoint, the UK's leading youth homelessness charity, have launched a major Christmas campaign calling on communities across the country to support young people facing homelessness this winter. The campaign marks the latest phase of Newsquest's year-long partnership with Centrepoint, which began in January when Newsquest announced a commitment to provide at least £4 million of advertising support across its print and digital portfolio during 2026. Throughout the year, the partnership has used Newsquest's extensive network of local news brands to raise awareness of youth homelessness and Centrepoint's work, alongside opportunities for fundraising and wider support. Now, as Christmas approaches, Newsquest and Centrepoint are building on that work with a dedicated national Christmas campaign focused on both immediate support for young people facing homelessness and the need for longer-term change. At the heart of the campaign is a simple appeal to readers. A £20 gift could provide vital food and toiletries for a young person facing homelessness this Christmas, in the form of an emergency hardship voucher. Alongside the fundraising appeal, the campaign will encourage people to support Centrepoint's wider campaigning work to help create lasting change for young people. The Christmas campaign has deliberately been developed around the principle that homelessness does not end when Christmas does, connecting immediate winter support with Centrepoint's longer-term work to help young people move towards stable housing. Newsquest titles across the country will support the campaign through print, digital and social content, with central campaign material complemented by local stories and opportunities in selected communities to bring the issue of youth homelessness closer to readers. Henry Faure Walker, CEO of Newsquest, said: "We have been incredibly proud to support Centrepoint throughout 2026 and, as the largest local media group, to use the reach of our news brands and local journalism to help shine a light on youth homelessness. "As we approach Christmas, we want to build on everything we have done together this year and give our readers another opportunity to make a difference. "Christmas should be a time of safety and hope, yet too many young people face the reality of homelessness. "Our titles sit at the heart of communities across the UK, and I hope that by working together we can encourage people to support Centrepoint this Christmas while continuing to raise awareness of the longer-term challenge of ending youth homelessness." Seyi Obakin, Chief Executive Officer at Centrepoint, said: “This Christmas, we're proud to be partnering with Newsquest to support young people facing homelessness. "For a young person with nowhere safe to stay, immediate support can make all the difference, whether that's a safe place to sleep, or someone to turn to in a crisis. "Homelessness doesn't end when Christmas does. A home is more than just a roof over your head. "It's the foundation from which young people can build their lives, their relationships, their careers, and their dreams for the future. "With the support of Newsquest and their readers, we can provide emergency help and open a door for more young people to thrive and build a future beyond homelessness.” The Christmas campaign will include a programme of editorial storytelling with a stronger winter focus, including young people's experiences and insight into Centrepoint's frontline work. The campaign will run across Newsquest's network of news brands in the weeks leading up to Christmas and into December. Will you be supporting Newsquest and Centrepoint's Christmas campaign? metadata.title: Drivers warned easy £10 fix could help avoid £2,500 fine and 3 points on licence
metadata.contentSnippet: This simple £10 fix could correct a common vehicle problem and reduce a driver's risk of receiving a £2,500 fine and three points.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Drivers warned easy £10 fix could help avoid £2,500 fine and 3 points on licence
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Drivers are being warned about a £2,500 fine which they could receive if they don't make an easy £10 fix. While you won't use your windscreen wipers on every outing, they certainly come in handy on wet days and when you need to improve your vision by clearing the windscreen. If you have damaged or broken windscreen wipers, it's important they're replaced because, as John Hood, the general manager at Auction4Cars.com explains, they can result in a £2,500 fine and three points on your licence. The vehicle company surveyed 2,000 UK drivers and found that almost a fifth of them (19%) have admitted to driving with broken or damaged windscreen wipers. Did you know how to spot when your wiper blades need replacing? (Image: Getty) Auction4Cars.com said that many drivers get behind the wheel despite their vehicles having common defects. Mr Hood said: "Autumn is one of the worst times of year for visibility on the road. "Rainy weather and spray from other vehicles puts more demand on your wipers, so it's important that they work properly. "If your wipers don't clear your windscreen well, you're putting yourself and other road users at risk. "Getting caught with worn-out wipers could land you a £2,500 fine and three points on your licence." If you're not sure if your windscreen wipers need replacing, Mr Hood has shared some advice to help you notice when they aren't up to scratch. He said: "If your wipers leave smears, make a squeaking noise or miss patches on your windscreen, it's usually a sign the blades are worn out. "Look for fraying or cracks in the rubber – these can stop the blades from clearing water effectively." Mr Hood said that, while you'll need to take into account how often the vehicle is used and what the weather has been like, "as a general rule, drivers should replace them every six months to a year". He said they're usually around £10 to replace and "compared to the cost of an MOT retest or a fine, it's a small price to pay that can make a huge difference to visibility, especially in the autumn months." The RAC added: "When you lift the wiper off the glass and you see that the rubber looks cracked, split, or is beginning to peel away from the frame, this means that the blades won't make proper contact with the windscreen and need replacing. "Finally, if you are driving during heavy rain and you have reduced visibility even if the wipers are moving, then it is important not to ignore it. "This is because worn wipers can seriously compromise safety. "Regular car maintenance involves checking the blades and cleaning them can extend their life, but once they show visible wear, replacement is the safest option." The RAC also shared a step-by-step guide for anyone who needs to replace their windscreen wipers. Lift the wiper arm away from the windscreen so that it locks and is upright, then find the release clip and either press or slide it to take the old wiper blade away. The RAC warns: "Carefully remove it, making sure the bare metal arm doesn't snap back onto the glass as this could cause several issues." Recommended reading: Then you'll need to "align the new blade with the hook or connector and push it into place until you hear a click." Once this is done, you need to "gently" return the wiper arm to the windscreen and then do the same again with the other blade if you're replacing both. When you have finished adding new blades, test them by using washer fluid so you can see if the wiper blades move over the windscreen correctly. Did you know windscreen wiper blades should be replaced every six to 12 months? Let us know in the comments below.

metadata.title: Airline used by Jet2 and TUI ceases operations after 16 years in sudden closure
metadata.contentSnippet: Slovakian airline AirExplore ceased operations on November 10, 2026, ending ACMI flights for UK carriers Jet2 and TUI.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Airline used by Jet2 and TUI ceases operations after 16 years in sudden closure
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A European airline that operated flights for UK carriers, including Jet2 and TUI, has ceased operations after 16 years. AirExplore, based in Slovakia, was founded in 2008 and began ACMI (wet leasing) operations in 2010. It provided aircraft and crew to UK carriers, including Jet2 and TUI, through ACMI  arrangements, helping support services across the UK and Europe. AirExplore aircraft have been seen at major UK airports, including Manchester, Bristol, Newcastle International, and London Stansted. The airline was acquired by Avia Solutions Group in June 2023. AirExplore officially ceased operations on Tuesday (November 10) and submitted a request to surrender its Air Operator Certificate (AOC). In a statement posted on its website, the airline said: "The Slovakian ACMI and charter airline AirExplore has ceased operations on 10 November 2026 and has submitted a request to surrender its Air Operator Certificate (AOC). "We thank all our employees, customers, partners, and team for their support over the years." No reason has been given for the closure. Meanwhile, UK-based Global Airlines has been ordered into compulsory liquidation. The UK startup, which planned to use a fleet of Airbus A380 planes, was formally ordered to wind up by the Insolvency and Companies Court on Wednesday (November 4), according to The Gazette. The winding-up petition was originally filed in May, with several hearings taking place in the following months, including the most recent in October. With the order now in place, an officer of the court, known as the official receiver, has taken control of winding up the company. Government guidelines state that once a winding-up order is issued, the company’s bank accounts are typically frozen and its assets sold off to repay creditors. Companies have the right to apply for cancellation of a winding-up order within five working days if they believe the action is unwarranted. Global Airlines is still listed as "active" on Companies House, though its most recent accounts are overdue. Global Airlines has been contacted for comment. Four other UK airlines have fallen into administration or liquidation this year: They join a growing list of UK travel companies that have ceased trading or entered administration/liquidation in 2026, including: Wayfairer Travel Limited has also suspended all services "until further notice" as it looks to appoint an administrator. metadata.title: Met Office forecasts snow for the UK in coming days - where 9cm per hour could fall
metadata.contentSnippet: The Met Office has forecast snow from Monday (November 16), with falls expected in Scotland, Wales, and northern England - see exactly where.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Met Office forecasts snow for the UK in coming days - where 9cm per hour could fall
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Snow has been forecast across parts of the UK early next week, with some areas set for falls of up to 9cm per hour. The Met Office has forecast "wintry showers", along with hill snow, and strong coastal winds between Monday (November 16) and Wednesday (November 18). The forecast reads: "Sunny for most on Monday, but wintry showers over northeast Scotland and rain for the southwest later. "From Tuesday, rain, hill snow in the north, showers, and strong coastal winds." Are you hoping for some snow?☃️ Colder air will make a return next week, but this time it will be joined by more unsettled weather. This means there is likely to be some snow in places. How much and where is still uncertain but there is the potential for some disruption due to snow and ice. — Met Office (@metoffice) November 13, 2026 Snow is expected to fall in the Scottish Highlands as early as Sunday (November 14), according to WX Charts weather maps. By late Monday, snow could move into South Wales around Merthyr Tydfil before spreading north overnight toward Newtown and Welshpool. Early Tuesday (November 17) could see further snowfall in parts of Yorkshire, Cumbria, and southern Scotland, reaching as far as Glasgow and Stirling. The most widespread snowfall across the UK is expected early on Tuesday (November 17). (Image: WX Charts) WX charts shows snow lingering around small areas of Scotland until the following Wednesday (November 25). This is likely to be the only snow the UK sees for the rest of November, according to the Met Office. The Met Office’s long-range forecast (for November 19 to 28) suggests a mix of rain and showers, particularly in the south and west, with drier, colder spells in between. The forecast reads: "A changeable pattern is likely to continue, with areas of rain or showers affecting parts of the UK, particularly across the south and west. "These will be interspersed with drier, colder interludes as shorter-lived ridges of high pressure develop. "Weather patterns may become slower evolving during the latter stages of November, leading to some uncertainty over how much progress Atlantic frontal systems will make into the UK. "Nonetheless, further rain or showers are likely at times, with the potential for some periods of strong winds. "Incursions of milder air are likely towards the south, although it could remain on the cold side overall further north, where there is potential for overnight frosts and occasional wintry precipitation, particularly over higher ground." Cold weather health alerts have also been issued for large parts of the UK. During winter, lots of illnesses like flu, and COVID-19 spread easily. If you're unwell, there are actions you can take to reduce the risk of spreading infections to others. 🤒 https://t.co/8hdhDCK9wS — UK Health Security Agency (@UKHSA) November 13, 2026 The warnings are expected to affect the North West, West Midlands, and Yorkshire and the Humber from 9pm on Sunday (November 15) until 9am on Thursday (November 19). The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said the alerts mean the weather is likely to have minor impacts on health and social care services, including an increased use of healthcare services and a greater risk to life to vulnerable people. Paul Coleman, consultant in public health at the UKHSA, said: "This is the latest Cold-Health Alert of the season, and we can expect more as we move further into winter. "Cold weather can have a serious impact on the health of some people, including those aged 65 and over and those with pre-existing health conditions, so it is vital to check in on friends, family and neighbours who are most vulnerable." Mr Coleman said people should try to keep the rooms they use most heated and dress warmly during colder spells. Is there snow forecast near you this week? Let us know in the comments below.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Two businesses making waves in manufacturing and fresh produce recently welcomed a visit from the mayor. Paul Bristow, mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, toured AMFRESH and Encocam at Alconbury Weald in Huntingdonshire to see first-hand how these companies are contributing to the region’s economy through innovation and industry partnerships. AMFRESH, a family-owned Spanish company with a presence in Peterborough, operates a packhouse and laboratory focused on citrus fruits, grapes, juices and other fresh produce. Matvii Smirnov, innovation director at AMFRESH, said: "We were delighted to welcome Paul Bristow and his team to our OMEGA Innovation Centre and to see the strong interest from the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Combined Authority in our efforts to deliver the highest quality and nutritional value to consumers." The company recently opened its OMEGA centre, which is dedicated to advancing fruit biochemistry and packing technology. Mr Bristow praised the company’s approach. He said: "It's great to see such innovation happening in our agri-tech sector. "AMFRESH is working with local schools, training skilled young people and contributing towards our regional economy." Encocam, a globally recognised advanced manufacturing business, focusing on automotive safety technologies and advanced engineering, was the mayor’s second stop. During his visit, Mr Bristow toured Encocam’s crash test dummy facility and discussed opportunities and challenges facing the automotive sector. Mayor Paul Bristow with James French at Encocam (Image: Combined Authority) Chris Hartley, HR manager at Encocam and a former apprentice, highlighted the company’s commitment to skills development. He said: "I continued my development with the support of some amazing workplace mentors and module tutors at Cambridge Regional College. "We see great potential in all our young people and recognise their importance to the future of our business. "That’s why we strive to give them the best support and training opportunities." Encocam has delivered more than 20 apprenticeship schemes over the past decade.

metadata.title: Cambs libraries not removing David Walliams books, council confirms
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire libraries will not be actively removing David Walliams’ books from their shelves, Cambridgeshire County Council has confirmed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambs libraries not removing David Walliams books, council confirms
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire libraries will not be actively removing David Walliams’ books from their shelves, the council has confirmed. Cambridgeshire County Council said its libraries will not be taking action to withdraw the author’s titles after an ITV News and The Guardian investigation saw him accused of sexual misconduct this week. Mr Walliams, 55, known for titles such as The Boy in the Dress and Gangsta Granny, wrote more than 40 books, which generated a revenue of £100 million by 2019. He has been accused of inappropriate sexual behaviour with girls allegedly as young as 15. He has also been accused of inappropriate conduct and sexual harassment at his former publisher HarperCollins, and while working on Britain’s Got Talent. Mr Walliams has denied all allegations of misconduct. Cambridgeshire County Council confirmed that Cambridgeshire Libraries "will not be actively removing" his books. A council spokesperson said: “Cambridgeshire Libraries is part of Libraries Connected, the body which represents all Public Library Services in England. "Libraries Connected has issued the below statement, which is consistent with our own Stock Policy, and specifically addresses the writings of David Walliams." Libraries Connected, which represents public library services across England, said that while all books should be available unless illegal, stock is routinely refreshed based on demand. Libraries Connected said: "In this case, we understand that demand for Walliams’s books has fallen significantly in recent years. "We would therefore expect the number of copies in circulation to decline naturally as they are replaced by newer and more popular titles, particularly as he is now without a publisher." Decisions about whether to keep Mr Walliams' books in Cambridgeshire schools will be made by governing bodies or trustee boards, the council confirmed. The council added that should the Department for Education issue any guidance, this would be shared with schools.

Weekly Family Update - 16.10.26 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What 
Matters Most 
Our virtue this week was Passion - going above and beyond what is expected. Our focus was: 
"We show focus and use positive language." Students explored the importance of speaking 
respectfully to adults and one another, using polite language and good manners, including 
phrases such as "excuse me", "please" and "thank you". 
Our Welfare Wednesday message focused on staying safe when travelling to and from 
school. Students were reminded to stay alert, particularly when crossing roads, and to avoid 
distractions such as headphones and mobile phones. We also spoke to cyclists about the 
importance of wearing a helmet and ensuring their bicycle is safe and roadworthy. 
This message is especially important at the moment as our building project continues to 
make excellent progress. While the work is carefully managed, we continue to remind 
students to stay aware of their surroundings, follow designated routes and make sensible 
choices around the site. The same focus, awareness and responsibility that keeps students 
safe on their journey to school is equally important during the school day. 
There will be no Weekly Update next week. Instead, we will be sharing our Half-Term 
Community Round-Up, celebrating the many achievements, events and successes from 
across the school this half term. 
Have a lovely weekend. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher

parents, guardians, and staff travelling to and from the school. There will be diversions in

Ensuring Pupils Feel Safe and Behave Well 
Safety First 
Road Safety 
Students were reminded this week about safe travel, including road safety, cycling safety, bus 
behaviour and remaining aware of their surroundings. 
The importance of respectful behaviour on school transport and safe travel was reinforced. 
Useful Resources 
• THINK!: https://www.think.gov.uk 
• Bikeability: https://www.bikeability.org.uk 
• Brake: https://www.brake.org.uk 
• Child Accident Prevention Trust: https://capt.org.uk 
If you need support or have any concerns about your child's wellbeing or safety, please 
contact welfare@abbey.college 
Police Liaison Officer Visits to School 
We are pleased to welcome Hannah Watkins, our School Liaison Officer, who visits school 
regularly. Hannah works closely with local secondary schools and provides valuable support 
to students, families and staff. 
Having a visible police presence in school helps students build positive relationships with 
local police officers, promotes trust and confidence, and provides an additional source of 
support and advice for young people. Hannah can also support the school with safeguarding 
concerns, advice around community issues affecting young people, and welfare checks 
where appropriate. 
We believe these visits are a positive addition to our school community and help strengthen 
links between school, families and local services, ensuring that our students feel safe, 
supported and well-informed. If you do have any questions or concerns regarding these 
visits please get in touch with the welfare team: welfare@abbey.college 
Promoting Positive Behaviour Every Day 
Neutral Behaviour Events 
We have added ‘neutral’ behaviour events to MCAS to help keep you informed. 
Please do not worry. These are not sanctions. It is simply a way for us to keep you informed 
when your child has received some extra support linked to their behaviour or attendance.  
If you have questions about these, please contact your child's form tutor. 

Student attendance  
Week 6 – Persistent Absence (PA) & Life Chances  
Missing just a few days each term soon adds up and can seriously impact your future.  
Students with lower attendance are more likely to struggle with exams and next steps.  
Aim high, 6 days or lesson off per year gives you the best chance of success.  
Ms Davis – Attendance Officer

Weekly Family Update - 06.11.26 
 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What 
Matters Most 
It has been lovely to welcome students back after the half-term break, and we have had a positive start 
to the new half term. 
We started the new half term by focusing on the virtue of Humility: “We accept praise, recognise others 
and apologise immediately.” 
Mrs Noble also led our Reset Assemblies, giving students time to celebrate what went well last half term 
and think about what they can do even better. We were delighted that every year group achieved our 
minimum 12:1 Spirit Ratio, earning their non-uniform rewards. Our aim is for every year group to achieve 
this again this half term. 
For Welfare Wednesday, students explored anti-social behaviour and the impact our actions can have on 
others. With darker evenings and events such as firework displays taking place, we asked students to 
show maturity and emotional intelligence when out in the community. How we behave matters, and we 
want our students to help others feel safe and respected. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher

Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters Most It has been lovely to welcome students back after the half-term break, and we have had a positive start to the new half term. We started the new half term by focusing on the virtue of Humility: “We accept praise, recognise others and apologise immediately.” Mrs Noble also led our Reset Assemblies, giving students time to celebrate what went well last half term and think about what they can do even better. We were delighted that every year group achieved our minimum 12:1 Spirit Ratio, earning their non-uniform rewards. Our aim is for every year group to achieve this again this half term. For Welfare Wednesday, students explored anti-social behaviour and the impact our actions can have on others. With darker evenings and events such as firework displays taking place, we asked students to show maturity and emotional intelligence when out in the community. How we behave matters, and we want our students to help others feel safe and respected. Andy Christoforou, Headteacher Please read on for essential updates. Weekly Family Update - 13.11.26 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters Most 
Remembrance Day: A Moment of Unity 
Remembrance has been marked with great care across our school this week.  
On Wednesday 11 November, our whole school came together to observe a two-minute silence for 
Armistice Day. Students who are members of the CCF, other local cadet forces and Scouts also wore 
their uniforms, adding a special connection to the occasion. Mr Patterson delivered a powerful 
speech, followed by readings from our Year 8 pupils, who had written their own poems. A selection of 
these is shared below. 
Remembrance gives us time to pause, reflect and come together. The respect shown by our students 
and staff is always moving and reflects the values we share as a school community. 
Every Day at School Matters 
Term 2 is short, with an INSET day on Friday 27 November. We expect all students to attend every 
school day through to the end of term on Friday 18 December. 
You can check our full term dates here. Please check these dates before making plans and do not 
book holidays during term time. 
Every day at school matters.  
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher

Knowing When to Seek Help 
This week students were reminded to trust their instincts. If a situation feels wrong, unsafe or

The message focused on trusting instincts, identifying trusted adults and understanding that

news.content: Weekly Family Update - 13.11.26 Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters Most Remembrance Day: A Moment of Unity Remembrance has been marked with great care across our school this week. On Wednesday 11 November, our whole school came together to observe a two-minute silence for Armistice Day. Students who are members of the CCF, other local cadet forces and Scouts also wore their uniforms, adding a special connection to the occasion. Mr Patterson delivered a powerful speech, followed by readings from our Year 8 pupils, who had written their own poems. A selection of these is shared below. Remembrance gives us time to pause, reflect and come together. The respect shown by our students and staff is always moving and reflects the values we share as a school community. Eve
